detector: (url matches //login/ in frame content OR alert matching /(?i)session has expired/ is present)

goal: Open a new sub-account for member 12345 with product code HSA and an initial deposit of 60.00. Complete the opening: confirm it and reach the screen that shows the new account number.

reason: Open Member Search to locate the member whose sub-account we need to open
Enter the member id so the search finds the correct member
Run the search to open the member's record
Open the matched member's profile to access sub-account actions
Start the sub-account opening flow for this member
Select the requested product type for the new sub-account
Enter the requested opening deposit amount for the new account
Proceed to the review step of the sub-account opening
Confirm the sub-account opening so the new account is created and its number is issued
The new account number is the answer the caller needs from this opening
Capture the confirmed opening balance as proof the deposit posted as requested

The "Sub-Account Opened" screen shows the status message "Sub-account opened successfully." with new account number 200050001 for member 12345, product HSA, opening balance $60.00 — the opening is confirmed and complete.

summary: 0 outcome(s) added, 1 rejected as unmatched, 8 checkpoint concern(s)
rejected: SUBACCOUNT_OPENED (matches the success screen -- it describes success, and the ladder would return it instead of Success)
concerns: s1: The OR branch 'button named "Search" is present' is very weak: a Search button appears on almost every list/lookup screen in this application, so this checkpoint would pass even if the navigation landed somewhere other than Member Search. The URL match alone is the meaningful half; the button alternative lets a wrong landing page through.

s3: Checking only that the URL is /members/search proves the search was submitted, not that a member was matched. A zero-result or ambiguous-result search sits on the same URL and would pass this checkpoint, pushing the real answer downstream where it surfaces as a confusing navigation failure at s4 instead of a business outcome. This step needs a positive assertion that a result row for the requested member id is present.

s4: The pattern /members/\d+$/ confirms some member profile opened but not that it is the member that was searched for. If the search result list ordering changes or a partial match is auto-opened, the flow would proceed to open a sub-account on the wrong member and still pass every remaining checkpoint.

s5: The OR branch 'button named "Continue" is present' is too weak to distinguish the sub-account opening form from any other multi-step form in the app; it would pass on an unrelated wizard page. It also gives no signal if the member is ineligible and the form is not offered.

s6: No checkpoint at all after selecting the product code. If the requested product code is not in the list (or the selection silently does not apply), the flow continues and can open an account under the wrong product, with no step ever detecting it. A checkpoint asserting the selected product value is needed.

s7: No checkpoint after entering the deposit amount. A rejected or reformatted amount (minimum-deposit rules, formatting) would go unnoticed here; any resulting validation message on the review step is not checked either.

s8: Relying solely on the presence of a button named 'Confirm and Open Account' is brittle to cosmetic label changes (e.g. 'Confirm & Open Account' or re-casing) and it also asserts nothing about the reviewed values — it would pass on a review page showing the wrong product or deposit.

s9: This is the most important checkpoint and the OR makes it unsafe: the URL branch /subaccount/confirm$ is reached merely by submitting the confirmation, so a rejected or failed opening that re-renders the same URL would be reported as success. It also never asserts that a new account number is present, which is the stated purpose of the flow. This should require the 'Sub-account opened successfully.' status (and ideally the account number) with no URL-only fallback.
